messages:
alex kim: Running a wide sweep this morning (LL & LL128, proto=LL/LL128, algo=RING/TREE) on the 8xA100 racks. Seeing weird mid-seq all-reduce spikes around tokens 256-512 that don't match our earlier baseline. Posting profiler snippets and experiment notes.
nina rao: can you paste the exact command you ran? also which runtime commit/sha?
alex kim: Commit: a7c3f2b (last stable perf before the recent kernel selection changes). Command:
```
./run_profiler --gpus=8 --batch_size=1 --seq=512 \
  --nccl_channels=4 --nccl_algo=RING --nccl_proto=LL128 \
  --affinity=compact --run=throughput_latency --log=prof.json
```
dmitri gordon: did you try toggling NCCL_ALGO or proto? LL128 has known path-dep issues with small collectives occasionally.
alex kim: Yeah. Baseline (old kernel selector) with NCCL_PROTO=LL + ALGO=RING was clean. After the kernel-selection optimizer landed, switching to LL128 reduces compute time but increases all-reduce wall time at those mid seq ranges. Trace shows full-synchronization points aligning with KV cache refills & prefix batching boundary.
rajiv s: can you share the perf numbers? rough token/ms or allreduce us per-step?
alex kim: From driver traces (avg over 100 steps):
- proto=LL, algo=RING: allreduce median = 210us, p95=340us
- proto=LL128, algo=RING: allreduce median = 280us, p95=620us (long tail)
- proto=LL128, algo=TREE: allreduce median = 260us, p95=400us

So LL128+RING gives biggest tails. CPU-side scheduling shows a burst of tiny CUDA kernels around the same time which suggests comm/compute overlap loss.
perf-bot: profiler run complete: throughput drop 9.8% vs baseline; detailing hotspots in /mnt/prof/runs/1771003333/ (uploaded)
nina rao: interesting that TREE reduces tail. Could be channel selection + algorithm interplay. How many channels per peer? you used 4, right?
alex kim: yes 4. Tried 8 channels as well — p95 improved a bit but median nudged up. Weirdly increasing channels increased kernel dispatch pressure on small kernels, which may hurt CPU scheduling.
dmitri gordon: hypothesis: Our kernel selector picked a different fused kernel layout for attention (smaller per-chunk kernels) that increases the number of CUDA launches per step and shifts the comm windows. LL128 expects larger contiguous messages to be efficient; with more launches we end up with fragmented buffers causing NCCL to fall back internally or do extra buffering.
rajiv s: can we validate by forcing the old kernel layout? Run with KERNEL_DISPATCH=legacy for a quick comparison.
alex kim: ran that. Legacy dispatch + LL128 + RING -> allreduce median 225us p95 360us. So it's definitely an interaction between new dispatch + LL128.
nina rao: steps to mitigate?
dmitri gordon: a few things to try (in order):
1) Force NCCL_PROTO=LL (fallback to smaller messages) to avoid internal LL128 buffering oddities.
2) Try NCCL_ALGO=TREE which you already saw helps.
3) Increase aggregation window in our batching heuristic (prefix bundling) to produce larger contiguous payloads.
4) Reduce number of NCCL channels so we don't overwhelm CPU with kernel launches (NCCL_CHANNELS=2-3 range).
5) Set NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=PARALLEL and NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 when testing to reduce CPU stalls.
alex kim: quick notes from trying 1-4:
- NCCL_PROTO=LL: restores baseline almost exactly. No long tails.
- NCCL_CHANNELS=2 with LL128: reduced p95 from 620us -> 420us, median ~260us.
- Batching window +10%: reduced KV cache refill alignment but slightly increased latency due to larger prefix merges.
rajiv s: so we have a tradeoff: LL128 gives compute-side speedups but risks allreduce tails unless we change dispatch or chunking. Maybe add a runtime knob: prefer LL when per-step contiguous payload > X bytes; otherwise force LL.
alex kim: agreed. I can add a quick heuristic in the kernel selector: estimate aggregate comm size per allreduce (sum over partitions) and prefer `proto=LL128` only if > 64KB. Otherwise prefer LL. That threshold is tunable.
nina rao: also add an override flag in the runtime for experiments, and record telemetry: proto chosen, channels, payload bytes, allreduce p95. We can then run an automated grid to pick safe defaults per model/seq distribution.
perf-bot: scheduled nightly sweep (8xA100) with heuristics: proto-thresh=64KB; channels={2,4}; algo={RING,TREE}. Results will be in /mnt/prof/auto/1771003333/sweep-01 by tomorrow.
dmitri gordon: also consider per-layer algo selection; some layers have much larger grad tensors and could use LL128 while others use LL. But that adds complexity.
alex kim: yeah per-layer adds complexity but possible to do with a static table generated at compile/cold-start time. For now I'll implement the global threshold heuristic + telemetry.
rajiv s: small ask: open a perf regression issue with the diff and tag kernel-selector change and include the trace you posted. We should bisect to confirm no other factors.
alex kim: filed issue #INF-1029 and attached traces + experiment commands. Assigning to eng-runtime to triage. I'll push a draft PR for the heuristic today and request review.
nina rao: thanks alex. If the nightly sweep shows a clear sweet spot we can bake that as default in the release candidate.
infra-bot: deployment note: cluster nodes used for sweep will be available 03:00 UTC; please avoid heavy jobs then. :warning:
alex kim: noted, thanks. I'll follow up with the PR link when ready.
